name: Barossa Valley
summary: A warm valley with a Mediterranean climate of cool, wet winters and warm, dry summers, on soils from clay loam to sand. It is known for full bodied, ripe Shiraz, some from very old vines.
label_note: A wine labelled with Barossa Valley as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Barossa Valley GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: Some vineyards are among the oldest Shiraz plantings in the world.

grapes.name: Mourvèdre
grapes.local_note: Known locally as Mataro.

name: McLaren Vale
summary: A warm Mediterranean region on the coast south of Adelaide, cooled by sea breezes and set on very varied soils. Its Shiraz is rich and medium to full bodied, often with chocolate notes, and old vine Grenache grows on sand.
label_note: A wine labelled with McLaren Vale as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the McLaren Vale GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: Often shows dark chocolate and blue fruit notes.

grapes.name: Grenache
grapes.local_note: Prized from old vines on sandy soils.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: The most planted white grape.

name: Clare Valley
summary: A valley in the northern Mount Lofty Ranges where warm days give way to cold nights and afternoon breezes, on varied soils that include slate. It is best known for dry, lime scented Riesling, alongside Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon.
pairing: Dry Riesling with shellfish, seafood and Asian dishes.
label_note: A wine labelled with Clare Valley as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Clare Valley GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Riesling
grapes.local_note: Made dry, with lime and citrus notes.

name: Coonawarra
summary: A cool region with a maritime influence in the south east of South Australia, known for a narrow strip of red terra rossa soil over limestone. Its Cabernet Sauvignon shows blackcurrant and plum fruit, and the best wines age well.
label_note: A wine labelled with Coonawarra as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Coonawarra GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
grapes.local_note: The region's main grape, with blackcurrant and plum fruit.

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: Lighter than Shiraz from warmer South Australian regions.

name: Adelaide Hills
summary: A cool, elevated region in the Mount Lofty Ranges east of Adelaide, mostly on loamy sands and loams over clay. Grapes keep good natural acidity, giving fresh Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and sparkling wine.
label_note: A wine labelled with Adelaide Hills as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Adelaide Hills GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: A cool climate style.

appellations.name: Lenswood
appellations.note: A cool subregion known for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

appellations.name: Piccadilly Valley
appellations.note: A cool, high and wet subregion known for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir.

name: Hunter
summary: A warm, humid region where cloud cover and sea breezes temper the heat. Its Semillon, grown on sandy alluvial flats, is picked early, low in alcohol and unoaked, and can age for decades; its Shiraz is medium bodied.
pairing: Young Semillon with seafood such as prawns, crab and white fish.
label_note: A wine labelled with Hunter as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Hunter GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Semillon
grapes.local_note: Picked early, low in alcohol and unoaked; can age for decades.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: Stone fruit and peach flavours.

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: Medium bodied, turning earthy with age.

appellations.name: Pokolbin
appellations.note: Official subregion of the Hunter, entered in the Register on 29 July 2010.

appellations.name: Broke Fordwich
appellations.note: Official subregion of the Hunter, entered in the Register on 2 September 1997.

appellations.name: Upper Hunter Valley
appellations.note: Official subregion of the Hunter, entered in the Register on 29 July 2010.

name: Yarra Valley
summary: A cool region east of Melbourne, with grey brown sandy loam on the northern side of the valley and red volcanic soil on the southern side. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay lead, and the Pinot Noir is light to medium bodied.
label_note: A wine labelled with Yarra Valley as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Yarra Valley GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: Light to medium bodied.

grapes.name: Shiraz
grapes.local_note: A lighter, more medium bodied style.

name: Margaret River
summary: A Mediterranean region with a strong maritime influence in the far south west of Western Australia, on gravelly, iron rich soils. Cabernet Sauvignon is its flagship red, alongside Chardonnay and crisp Semillon and Sauvignon Blanc blends.
label_note: A wine labelled with Margaret River as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Margaret River GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
grapes.local_note: The flagship red, often blended with Merlot.

grapes.name: Sauvignon Blanc
grapes.local_note: Often blended with Semillon.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: Much of it from the Gingin clone, with lime like acidity.

grapes.name: Semillon
grapes.local_note: Often blended with Sauvignon Blanc.

name: Tasmania
summary: The coolest and most southerly of Australia's wine regions, an island state with very varied soils. It is known for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay with high natural acidity, and traditional method sparkling wine made mainly from those two grapes.
label_note: A wine labelled with Tasmania as its only GI must contain at least 85% wine from grapes grown in the Tasmania GI (Wine Australia Regulations 2018, s 26(2)).

grapes.name: Pinot Noir
grapes.local_note: Fragrant and delicate, light to medium bodied; also a sparkling base.

grapes.name: Chardonnay
grapes.local_note: High natural acidity; also a sparkling base.
